analysis: The method overrides the clone() method from Object. It calls super.clone(), which can throw CloneNotSupportedException if the class does not implement the Cloneable interface. By catching this exception and throwing an AssertionError, the programmer indicates that the CloneNotSupportedException should never occur under normal circumstances, as the class is presumably designed to be cloneable (e.g., implements Cloneable). The throw of AssertionError is an assertion failure: it signals a bug in the program (e.g., the class not properly implementing Cloneable). AssertionError is an Error, not an Exception, and it is generally not intended to be caught by the caller; instead, it indicates a serious, unrecoverable condition that should propagate to the top-level thread handler or cause the program to terminate.
